strategies.description:
Holds the spot asset and shorts the perpetual against it, so the position has no view on the price, and collects the funding the shorts are paid while the perpetual trades above the spot. When funding falls far enough it unwinds, and when the vault falls far enough from its peak it only reduces.

The edge is mechanical and it compresses as more capital chases it, which is the honest thing to say about it: the record shows the size it was earned at, and a larger vault should expect less.
claims: Gross exposure at most twice the vault's value
No single order above 5% of the vault
6% of the vault kept liquid, so an ordinary withdrawal closes nothing
Only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak
One market, BTC against BTC-PERP, and nothing else

# Shonin Agents

The reference agents: WASM components compiled from this repository and published to a Shonin platform. An **agent** is the program; a **strategy** is what it is trying to do, and it is the word the platform's contracts use. See `README.md` for the layout and the quickstart.

## Rules

- **This repository is public.** Never mention other repositories, local paths or private projects in anything committed.
- **An agent's limits live in its own source**, as constants in `src/config.rs`, and are claimed in its manifest in the same words. There is no platform policy to defer to, and nothing here should read as if there were.
- **The SDK is a version, not a path.** `Cargo.toml` declares `shonin-strategy-sdk` by version; a local checkout is patched in through the gitignored `.cargo/config.toml` that `task patch` writes. Never commit a path dependency.
- **Dependencies live in the workspace.** Declare every version in `[workspace.dependencies]`; crates use `{ workspace = true }`.
- **An agent is reproducible or it is nothing.** `Cargo.lock` is committed and every build is `--locked`, so the bundle the build service signs is the one anybody else gets from the same source. Nothing here may read a clock, the network or a random number while it compiles: the reviewer reports that against the agent's reproducibility rating.
- **Nothing here holds a key.** An agent signs nothing and reads no secret it did not declare. If something looks like it needs a key, the design is wrong.

## Commit guard

Every commit runs `.githooks/commit-msg` (enabled by `task setup`). It rejects a commit whose message or staged changes contain a secret, a term from the local, gitignored `.private/terms.txt`, an absolute home path, or content a reviewer model judges to break the local policy in `.private/review.md`.

Never bypass it: no `--no-verify` or `-n`, no changes to `core.hooksPath`, no `SHONIN_SKIP_REVIEW`. When it blocks a commit, fix the commit. Never commit anything under `.private/`.

## Done means

`task check`, `task lint` and `task test` all pass, and `task build` produces a component.

# together; the build service supplies its own pinned copy the same way, so
# `--locked` holds on both sides.
shonin-strategy-sdk = "0.1.0"

futures = "0.3.34"
serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }

unsafe_code = "deny"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

[profile.release]
# An agent is a component the build service compiles from source with a
# pinned recipe, so the profile is part of what makes it reproducible.
opt-level = "s"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
strip = true

# Shonin Agents

The reference agents. Each one is a WASM component compiled from the Rust in this repository, published to a Shonin platform, and run by an attested executor that alone holds its vault's keys.

An agent here is an ordinary Rust library that implements one long-lived async function. It holds no key, signs nothing, and reaches the outside world only through the imports the `shonin:agent` world gives it. Whatever it decides, it can only ever trade its vault's own accounts.

## Prerequisites

- [Rust](https://rustup.rs). The toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`, with the `wasm32-wasip2` target an agent compiles to.
- [Task](https://taskfile.dev)
- For the commit guard: [gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks), [jq](https://jqlang.org) and the [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) CLI.

## Quickstart

```bash
task setup    # toolchain, commit guard, and the SDK pointed at a local platform
task build    # build every agent as a component
task check    # compile natively and as a component
task lint     # rustfmt --check + clippy -D warnings
task test     # native tests
task dev      # publish funding-basis to a platform running locally
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` first, and set `SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR` to a checkout of the platform. `task patch` writes a gitignored `.cargo/config.toml` that resolves the SDK from there while the SDK and the agents are moving together; without it, the SDK resolves from the registry by the version in `Cargo.toml`, which is what the build service does. `task dev` (or `task publish AGENT=<name>`) publishes through that checkout, to the platform its `task dev` is running: the platform's seed uploads the source, pays to publish it, and activates it once it is reviewed and built, the same flow its web app uses.

## The agents

| Agent | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `funding-basis` | Holds the spot asset, shorts the perpetual against it, and collects the funding between them. The position has no view on the price, so what is left is the carry. |

## Layout

```text
packages/
  agents/funding-basis/  the agent: its manifest, its settings in src/config.rs, and the code the reviewer reads
```

Each agent is a directory with a `Cargo.toml`, a `shonin.toml` and its source. The manifest only declares, for the platform: the chain its vault lives on, the author's description and claims, and the drivers it trades through. Its own settings are constants in `src/config.rs`, and its allowances are set on the vault when it is activated. The platform hashes the manifest, and a vault's page shows what it said.

## Limits live in the code

There is no platform risk policy, and there is nothing to configure that would add one. An agent's limits are written in its own source, claimed in its manifest in the same words, and checked against the code by the reviewer. A depositor comparing the page against the code is comparing two descriptions of one thing.

## License

Apache-2.0. These are examples: read them, copy them, publish your own.

# The agents: trading programs published to a running Shonin platform.
version: "3"
silent: true
dotenv: [".env"]

# `.env` is read into every command's environment, so the settings are read
# there rather than into Task's own variables: a variable computed with `sh:`
# runs before the file is loaded and would always come back empty.

tasks:
  default:
    cmds:
      - task --list

  setup:
    desc: "Install the toolchain, enable the commit guard, and point the SDK at a local platform"
    cmds:
      - rustup show active-toolchain || rustup toolchain install
      - git config core.hooksPath .githooks
      - |
        for bin in cargo gitleaks claude jq; do
          command -v "$bin" >/dev/null || echo "missing: $bin (see README.md)"
        done
        for f in .private/terms.txt .private/review.md; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || echo "missing: $f (commit guard input; commits are blocked until it exists)"
        done
      - task: patch

  patch:
    desc: "Point the SDK at a local platform checkout (SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR)"
    cmds:
      - |
        if [ -z "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR:-}" ]; then
          echo "SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR is unset: the SDK resolves from the registry."
          rm -f .cargo/config.toml
          exit 0
        fi
        mkdir -p .cargo
        cat > .cargo/config.toml <<EOF
        # Written by \`task patch\`; gitignored. The SDK is declared by version
        # in Cargo.toml and resolved from a checkout while the two move together.
        [patch.crates-io]
        shonin-strategy-sdk = { path = "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}/packages/strategy-sdk" }
        EOF
        echo "SDK patched to ${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}"

  build:
    desc: "Build every agent as a component"
    cmds:
      - cargo build --release --locked --target wasm32-wasip2 -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst

  publish:
    desc: "Publish an agent to a platform running locally (AGENT=funding-basis)"
    vars:
      AGENT: '{{.AGENT | default "funding-basis"}}'
    cmds:
      # The platform publishes it, from its own checkout, through the same flow
      # its web app uses: the vault is created, then the source goes to the
      # build service. Its seed reads the agents from this checkout.
      - |
        if [ -z "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR:-}" ]; then
          echo "Set SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR to a checkout of the platform (see .env.example)."
          exit 1
        fi
        SHONIN_AGENTS_DIR="$PWD" task -d "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}" services:seed AGENT="{{.AGENT}}"

  dev:
    desc: "Publish funding-basis to a platform running locally and follow the build"
    cmds:
      - task: publish

  check:
    desc: "Compile every crate, natively and as a component"
    cmds:
      - cargo check --workspace --all-targets
      - cargo check -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst --target wasm32-wasip2

  lint:
    desc: "rustfmt --check and clippy -D warnings"
    cmds:
      - cargo fmt --all --check
      - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - cargo clippy -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst --target wasm32-wasip2 -- -D warnings

  fmt:
    desc: "Format every crate"
    cmds:
      - cargo fmt --all

  test:
    desc: "Native tests"
    cmds:
      - cargo test --workspace

  clean:
    cmds:
      - cargo clean

findings.summary: The vault's peak, used for the 10% drawdown stop the manifest claims, is kept only in memory and is reset by a restart
findings.detail: Mind::new() in funding-basis sets `peak: Decimal::from(0)`, and `step()` immediately raises it to the current vault value on the next read (`if state.vault_value > mind.peak { mind.peak = state.vault_value; }`). If the agent (or its host) restarts while the vault is already down from its true peak, the new instance treats the current, already-depressed value as the peak, so `only_reducing()` in decide.rs never sees the real drawdown and the agent keeps opening new pairs instead of only reducing — exactly the behaviour the manifest says is bounded by '10% fall from the vault's peak'. The same pattern exists in the Hyperliquid variant (src/lib.rs Mind::new/step) and in weekend-carry (peak in Mind, updated in picture()). None of those manifests mention this restart caveat, unlike mm-quoter's manifest, which does disclose an analogous reset for its own counter.

findings.summary: Catalyst's per-position entry price/time, used for its stop-loss and hold-timer claims, is also rebuilt from 'now' after a restart
findings.detail: In `step()`, a position already held by the Safe but not yet tracked by this instance of `Mind` is inserted with `Entry { at: now(), price: price.market_price }` — the current time and current price, not the real entry. After a restart this both resets the 1-day hold timer (extending how long a position can be held past the claimed 'closed after a day') and re-bases the 3% stop-loss off the post-restart price rather than the true entry price, so a position already down close to 3% gets a fresh 3% of room to fall further before the stop fires. This is the same class of issue as the funding-basis peak reset above, applied to catalyst's own claims.

findings.summary: Workspace depends on a few lesser-known crates alongside the standard ones
findings.detail: Most of the pinned dependencies (serde, anyhow, futures, syn/quote/proc-macro2, the wit-bindgen/wasm-tooling family) are widely used. `bnum`, `fastnum` (used for the SDK's fixed-point `Decimal`) and `zmij` (a transitive dependency of serde_json 1.0.151) are comparatively obscure compared to alternatives in their space. The author's note says every crate is on the platform's own reviewed list by version and checksum, which mitigates but doesn't eliminate the exposure of depending on less-audited code for arithmetic that directly drives position sizing.

findings.summary: Price and funding data come from streams the same platform/author operates
findings.detail: funding-basis-hyperliquid reads its spot/perp order books and funding rate from 'Shonin's shared Hyperliquid stream' (HYPERLIQUID feed), and weekend-carry/mm-quoter read similarly from Shonin's shared Lighter/Hyperliquid streams. This is disclosed architecture (the README states the agent 'reaches the outside world only through the imports the shonin:agent world gives it'), and it is a reasonable platform design, but it does mean every agent's trading decisions ultimately depend on a feed the same organization that publishes the agent also operates and could, in principle, alter after publication.

findings.summary: The Hyperliquid variant trades a smaller, less liquid pair than the BTC agent the description names
findings.detail: The author's description and claims (at the top of this review) describe 'BTC against BTC-PERP.' The Hyperliquid variant in the same workspace instead trades HYPE/USDC spot against the HYPE perpetual (config.rs: SPOT = "HYPE/USDC", PERP = "HYPE"), a materially smaller-cap, less liquid market than BTC, with its own manifest separately describing and claiming the same percentage limits. Gross exposure and per-order caps are still enforced in code for this variant, but a thinner book makes the slippage assumptions (SLIPPAGE = 0.002) and the five-significant-figure price rounding more likely to be tested in practice than they would be for BTC.

review.summary:
The submitted project is a Rust/WASM workspace of five Shonin reference trading agents sharing one SDK. The one the author's description and claims refer to is "funding-basis": it holds spot BTC and shorts BTC-PERP through a "local" driver, opening and adding to the pair when funding exceeds an entry threshold and unwinding when funding falls below an exit threshold or the vault's value falls 10% from its peak. Sizing is computed in `decide.rs` as pure arithmetic (no I/O), bounded by a 5%-of-vault per-order cap and a 2x gross-leverage cap, with a 6% idle buffer kept in the vault and a "Patience" backoff so refused orders aren't resent every tick. The workspace also contains four other agents (a Hyperliquid HYPE variant of the same strategy, a market maker, a weekend stock-token/perp carry, and an SEC-filing-driven "Catalyst" agent using a placeholder linear model) that are not mentioned in the author's description but are part of the same submitted source.

The code is careful and its stated limits are genuinely computed and enforced in the decision logic (confirmed by the crate's own property tests), not just claimed in the manifest. The one structural weakness that recurs across every stateful agent in the repo is that risk state used to decide when to de-risk — the vault's peak value (for the 10% drawdown stop) in `funding-basis` and `weekend-carry`, and a position's entry price/time (for the 3%-stop/1-day-hold) in `catalyst` — lives only in memory. A restart resets these references to "now," so a vault already in a drawdown, or a position already stopped-out, gets treated as freshly healthy immediately after a restart, silently loosening the one backstop each agent's description relies on. This doesn't let position size or leverage exceed the hard caps (those are always re-derived and still enforced), but it does mean the drawdown/stop-loss claims are not restart-safe, and none of the manifests disclose that caveat (mm-quoter's manifest is the one place in the repo that does disclose an analogous restart reset, for its daily cancel-count).
limits: This review only read the Rust source, Cargo manifests/lockfile and TOML configuration provided; it did not have the shonin-strategy-sdk crate's own source, so SDK-level guarantees (e.g. how `Decimal`, `drivers::submit`, or the vault contract itself enforce anything) were taken on trust from how the agent code calls them, not independently verified.

The repository's `.private/terms.txt` and `.private/review.md`, referenced by CLAUDE.md as inputs to the commit guard, are gitignored and were not part of the submitted source, so their contents could not be checked.

No compiled WASM component, build logs, or running executor were available, so claims about reproducible builds and the wasm32-wasip2 target could only be checked by reading the manifests and `rust-toolchain.toml`, not by actually building.

This is a static reading of source code only; it cannot rule out behavior that depends on runtime data (live order books, funding rates, vault contract state) not present in the submitted files, and it is one reading of the code, not a proof of its properties.

# Shonin Agents

The reference agents: WASM components compiled from this repository and published to a Shonin platform. An **agent** is the program; a **strategy** is what it is trying to do, and it is the word the platform's contracts use. See `README.md` for the layout and the quickstart.

## Rules

- **This repository is public.** Never mention other repositories, local paths or private projects in anything committed.
- **An agent's limits live in its own source**, as constants in `src/config.rs`, and are claimed in its manifest in the same words. There is no platform policy to defer to, and nothing here should read as if there were.
- **The SDK is a version, not a path.** `Cargo.toml` declares `shonin-strategy-sdk` by version; a local checkout is patched in through the gitignored `.cargo/config.toml` that `task patch` writes. Never commit a path dependency.
- **Dependencies live in the workspace.** Declare every version in `[workspace.dependencies]`; crates use `{ workspace = true }`.
- **An agent is reproducible or it is nothing.** `Cargo.lock` is committed and every build is `--locked`, so the bundle the build service signs is the one anybody else gets from the same source. Nothing here may read a clock, the network or a random number while it compiles: the reviewer reports that against the agent's reproducibility rating.
- **Nothing here holds a key.** An agent signs nothing and reads no secret it did not declare. If something looks like it needs a key, the design is wrong.

## Commit guard

Every commit runs `.githooks/commit-msg` (enabled by `task setup`). It rejects a commit whose message or staged changes contain a secret, a term from the local, gitignored `.private/terms.txt`, an absolute home path, or content a reviewer model judges to break the local policy in `.private/review.md`.

Never bypass it: no `--no-verify` or `-n`, no changes to `core.hooksPath`, no `SHONIN_SKIP_REVIEW`. When it blocks a commit, fix the commit. Never commit anything under `.private/`.

## Done means

`task check`, `task lint` and `task test` all pass, and `task build` produces a component.

# Shonin Agents

The reference agents. Each one is a WASM component compiled from the Rust in this repository, published to a Shonin platform, and run by an attested executor that alone holds its vault's keys.

An agent here is an ordinary Rust library that implements one long-lived async function. It holds no key, signs nothing, and reaches the outside world only through the imports the `shonin:agent` world gives it. Whatever it decides, it can only ever trade its vault's own accounts.

## Prerequisites

- [Rust](https://rustup.rs). The toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`, with the `wasm32-wasip2` target an agent compiles to.
- [Task](https://taskfile.dev)
- For the commit guard: [gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks), [jq](https://jqlang.org) and the [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) CLI.

## Quickstart

```bash
task setup    # toolchain, commit guard, and the SDK pointed at a local platform
task build    # build every agent as a component
task check    # compile natively and as a component
task lint     # rustfmt --check + clippy -D warnings
task test     # native tests
task dev      # publish funding-basis to a platform running locally
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` first, and set `SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR` to a checkout of the platform. `task patch` writes a gitignored `.cargo/config.toml` that resolves the SDK from there while the SDK and the agents are moving together; without it, the SDK resolves from the registry by the version in `Cargo.toml`, which is what the build service does. `task dev` (or `task publish AGENT=<name>`) publishes through that checkout, to the platform its `task dev` is running: the platform's seed uploads the source, pays to publish it, and activates it once it is reviewed and built, the same flow its web app uses.

## The agents

| Agent | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `funding-basis` | Holds the spot asset, shorts the perpetual against it, and collects the funding between them. The position has no view on the price, so what is left is the carry. |

## Layout

```text
packages/
  agents/funding-basis/  the agent: its manifest, its settings in src/config.rs, and the code the reviewer reads
```

Each agent is a directory with a `Cargo.toml`, a `shonin.toml` and its source. The manifest only declares, for the platform: the chain its vault lives on, the author's description and claims, and the drivers it trades through. Its own settings are constants in `src/config.rs`, and its allowances are set on the vault when it is activated. The platform hashes the manifest, and a vault's page shows what it said.

## Limits live in the code

There is no platform risk policy, and there is nothing to configure that would add one. An agent's limits are written in its own source, claimed in its manifest in the same words, and checked against the code by the reviewer. A depositor comparing the page against the code is comparing two descriptions of one thing.

# `.env` is read into every command's environment, so the settings are read
# there rather than into Task's own variables: a variable computed with `sh:`
# runs before the file is loaded and would always come back empty.

tasks:
  default:
    cmds:
      - task --list

  setup:
    desc: "Install the toolchain, enable the commit guard, and point the SDK at a local platform"
    cmds:
      - rustup show active-toolchain || rustup toolchain install
      - git config core.hooksPath .githooks
      - |
        for bin in cargo gitleaks claude jq; do
          command -v "$bin" >/dev/null || echo "missing: $bin (see README.md)"
        done
        for f in .private/terms.txt .private/review.md; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || echo "missing: $f (commit guard input; commits are blocked until it exists)"
        done
      - task: patch

  patch:
    desc: "Point the SDK at a local platform checkout (SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR)"
    cmds:
      - |
        if [ -z "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR:-}" ]; then
          echo "SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR is unset: the SDK resolves from the registry."
          rm -f .cargo/config.toml
          exit 0
        fi
        mkdir -p .cargo
        cat > .cargo/config.toml <<EOF
        # Written by \`task patch\`; gitignored. The SDK is declared by version
        # in Cargo.toml and resolved from a checkout while the two move together.
        [patch.crates-io]
        shonin-strategy-sdk = { path = "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}/packages/strategy-sdk" }
        EOF
        echo "SDK patched to ${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}"

  build:
    desc: "Build every agent as a component"
    cmds:
      - cargo build --release --locked --target wasm32-wasip2 -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst

  publish:
    desc: "Publish an agent to a platform running locally (AGENT=funding-basis)"
    vars:
      AGENT: '{{.AGENT | default "funding-basis"}}'
    cmds:
      # The platform publishes it, from its own checkout, through the same flow
      # its web app uses: the vault is created, then the source goes to the
      # build service. Its seed reads the agents from this checkout.
      - |
        if [ -z "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR:-}" ]; then
          echo "Set SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR to a checkout of the platform (see .env.example)."
          exit 1
        fi
        SHONIN_AGENTS_DIR="$PWD" task -d "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}" services:seed AGENT="{{.AGENT}}"

  dev:
    desc: "Publish funding-basis to a platform running locally and follow the build"
    cmds:
      - task: publish

  check:
    desc: "Compile every crate, natively and as a component"
    cmds:
      - cargo check --workspace --all-targets
      - cargo check -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst --target wasm32-wasip2

  lint:
    desc: "rustfmt --check and clippy -D warnings"
    cmds:
      - cargo fmt --all --check
      - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - cargo clippy -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst --target wasm32-wasip2 -- -D warnings

  fmt:
    desc: "Format every crate"
    cmds:
      - cargo fmt --all

  test:
    desc: "Native tests"
    cmds:
      - cargo test --workspace

  clean:
    cmds:
      - cargo clean

# Shonin Agents

The reference agents: WASM components compiled from this repository and published to a Shonin platform. An **agent** is the program; a **strategy** is what it is trying to do, and it is the word the platform's contracts use. See `README.md` for the layout and the quickstart.

## Rules

- **This repository is public.** Never mention other repositories, local paths or private projects in anything committed.
- **An agent's limits live in its own source**, as constants in `src/config.rs`, and are claimed in its manifest in the same words. There is no platform policy to defer to, and nothing here should read as if there were.
- **The SDK is a version, not a path.** `Cargo.toml` declares `shonin-strategy-sdk` by version; a local checkout is patched in through the gitignored `.cargo/config.toml` that `task patch` writes. Never commit a path dependency.
- **Dependencies live in the workspace.** Declare every version in `[workspace.dependencies]`; crates use `{ workspace = true }`.
- **An agent is reproducible or it is nothing.** `Cargo.lock` is committed and every build is `--locked`, so the bundle the build service signs is the one anybody else gets from the same source. Nothing here may read a clock, the network or a random number while it compiles: the reviewer reports that against the agent's reproducibility rating.
- **Nothing here holds a key.** An agent signs nothing and reads no secret it did not declare. If something looks like it needs a key, the design is wrong.

## Commit guard

Every commit runs `.githooks/commit-msg` (enabled by `task setup`). It rejects a commit whose message or staged changes contain a secret, a term from the local, gitignored `.private/terms.txt`, an absolute home path, or content a reviewer model judges to break the local policy in `.private/review.md`.

Never bypass it: no `--no-verify` or `-n`, no changes to `core.hooksPath`, no `SHONIN_SKIP_REVIEW`. When it blocks a commit, fix the commit. Never commit anything under `.private/`.

## Done means

`task check`, `task lint` and `task test` all pass, and `task build` produces a component.

# Shonin Agents

The reference agents. Each one is a WASM component compiled from the Rust in this repository, published to a Shonin platform, and run by an attested executor that alone holds its vault's keys.

An agent here is an ordinary Rust library that implements one long-lived async function. It holds no key, signs nothing, and reaches the outside world only through the imports the `shonin:agent` world gives it. Whatever it decides, it can only ever trade its vault's own accounts.

## Prerequisites

- [Rust](https://rustup.rs). The toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`, with the `wasm32-wasip2` target an agent compiles to.
- [Task](https://taskfile.dev)
- For the commit guard: [gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks), [jq](https://jqlang.org) and the [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) CLI.

## Quickstart

```bash
task setup    # toolchain, commit guard, and the SDK pointed at a local platform
task build    # build every agent as a component
task check    # compile natively and as a component
task lint     # rustfmt --check + clippy -D warnings
task test     # native tests
task dev      # publish funding-basis to a platform running locally
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` first, and set `SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR` to a checkout of the platform. `task patch` writes a gitignored `.cargo/config.toml` that resolves the SDK from there while the SDK and the agents are moving together; without it, the SDK resolves from the registry by the version in `Cargo.toml`, which is what the build service does. `task dev` (or `task publish AGENT=<name>`) publishes through that checkout, to the platform its `task dev` is running: the platform's seed uploads the source, pays to publish it, and activates it once it is reviewed and built, the same flow its web app uses.

## The agents

| Agent | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `funding-basis` | Holds the spot asset, shorts the perpetual against it, and collects the funding between them. The position has no view on the price, so what is left is the carry. |

## Layout

```text
packages/
  agents/funding-basis/  the agent: its manifest, its settings in src/config.rs, and the code the reviewer reads
```

Each agent is a directory with a `Cargo.toml`, a `shonin.toml` and its source. The manifest only declares, for the platform: the chain its vault lives on, the author's description and claims, and the drivers it trades through. Its own settings are constants in `src/config.rs`, and its allowances are set on the vault when it is activated. The platform hashes the manifest, and a vault's page shows what it said.

## Limits live in the code

There is no platform risk policy, and there is nothing to configure that would add one. An agent's limits are written in its own source, claimed in its manifest in the same words, and checked against the code by the reviewer. A depositor comparing the page against the code is comparing two descriptions of one thing.

# The agents: trading programs published to a running Shonin platform.
version: "3"
silent: true
dotenv: [".env"]

# `.env` is read into every command's environment, so the settings are read
# there rather than into Task's own variables: a variable computed with `sh:`
# runs before the file is loaded and would always come back empty.

tasks:
  default:
    cmds:
      - task --list

  setup:
    desc: "Install the toolchain, enable the commit guard, and point the SDK at a local platform"
    cmds:
      - rustup show active-toolchain || rustup toolchain install
      - git config core.hooksPath .githooks
      - |
        for bin in cargo gitleaks claude jq; do
          command -v "$bin" >/dev/null || echo "missing: $bin (see README.md)"
        done
        for f in .private/terms.txt .private/review.md; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || echo "missing: $f (commit guard input; commits are blocked until it exists)"
        done
      - task: patch

  patch:
    desc: "Point the SDK at a local platform checkout (SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR)"
    cmds:
      - |
        if [ -z "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR:-}" ]; then
          echo "SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR is unset: the SDK resolves from the registry."
          rm -f .cargo/config.toml
          exit 0
        fi
        mkdir -p .cargo
        cat > .cargo/config.toml <<EOF
        # Written by \`task patch\`; gitignored. The SDK is declared by version
        # in Cargo.toml and resolved from a checkout while the two move together.
        [patch.crates-io]
        shonin-strategy-sdk = { path = "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}/packages/strategy-sdk" }
        EOF
        echo "SDK patched to ${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}"

  build:
    desc: "Build every agent as a component"
    cmds:
      - cargo build --release --locked --target wasm32-wasip2 -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst

  publish:
    desc: "Publish an agent to a platform running locally (AGENT=funding-basis)"
    vars:
      AGENT: '{{.AGENT | default "funding-basis"}}'
    cmds:
      # The platform publishes it, from its own checkout, through the same flow
      # its web app uses: the vault is created, then the source goes to the
      # build service. Its seed reads the agents from this checkout.
      - |
        if [ -z "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR:-}" ]; then
          echo "Set SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR to a checkout of the platform (see .env.example)."
          exit 1
        fi
        SHONIN_AGENTS_DIR="$PWD" task -d "${SHONIN_PLATFORM_DIR}" services:seed AGENT="{{.AGENT}}"

  dev:
    desc: "Publish funding-basis to a platform running locally and follow the build"
    cmds:
      - task: publish

  check:
    desc: "Compile every crate, natively and as a component"
    cmds:
      - cargo check --workspace --all-targets
      - cargo check -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst --target wasm32-wasip2

  lint:
    desc: "rustfmt --check and clippy -D warnings"
    cmds:
      - cargo fmt --all --check
      - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - cargo clippy -p funding-basis -p funding-basis-hyperliquid -p mm-quoter -p weekend-carry -p catalyst --target wasm32-wasip2 -- -D warnings

  fmt:
    desc: "Format every crate"
    cmds:
      - cargo fmt --all

  test:
    desc: "Native tests"
    cmds:
      - cargo test --workspace

  clean:
    cmds:
      - cargo clean
